The build process uses Cargo (Rust's package manager) in a controlled manner with --frozen and --locked flags, which prevent unexpected dependency changes.

The script defines functions and phases (prepare, build, check, package) that follow standard Rust packaging practices for AUR. It sets RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=stable for reproducibility but does not introduce any network requests, dynamic code evaluation, or file operations outside the build directory. All installed files are from the verified source and placed in appropriate system locations (e.g., /usr/bin, /usr/share). There are no signs of obfuscation, unexpected downloads, or data exfiltration.

The package depends only on standard system libraries (glibc, gcc-libs) and build-time Cargo, which is normal for Rust applications. The maintainer uses a predictable and transparent workflow without any red flags such as git pull at build time, base64-encoded payloads, or curl|bash patterns. The license (GPL-3.0-or-later) is open source and consistent with the project's stated goals.
</details>
